criteria.bundle_handle: Handle-scoped bundles: test::evidence_open returns an opaque bundle handle, test::evidence_append records named blobs into it, and test::evidence_seal finalizes it into digests plus a receipt kind from a closed set. Attestation covers precisely the appended content, so unrelated filesystem state can neither enter nor perturb the sealed receipt.
criteria.memory_only: No persistence operations: evidence never leaves Can values, and storage decisions belong entirely to the caller. This is the smallest possible change (none), but it yields no sealed owner-visible artifact and fragments the receipt vocabulary across callers.
criteria.path_seal: File-backed sealing: evidence lands through files::* wherever the test writes it, and one new test::evidence_seal operation digests a caller-supplied str[] of paths into a receipt kind. Mechanism cost is a single operation; robustness cost is that seal-time reads accept missing, substituted, or out-of-scope paths.

evidence_bundle.instructions: Select the receipt-production shape that attests qualified-report, n-receipt and cleanup-receipt evidence with digests at minimal mechanism cost.

criteria.grant_wrapped_reuse: Authorization wrapper: a new test::grant_process check permits individual process::run invocations that otherwise keep their unrestricted executable string. Nearly zero new surface, but authorization does not narrow expressiveness: arbitrary dispatch stays available to any holder of a live grant.
criteria.keyed_dispatch: Registry-keyed tools: test::run_tool names a tool through an owner-registered key and supplies argv/cwd/env/options; paths never appear in the call. Staged implements (bundled bun, formatter, built CLI) enter the per-grant registry up front, and unregistered keys refuse pre-spawn. Per-run dispatch vocabulary is finite and enumerable, with staging locations captured in the tool records.
criteria.workspace_relative: Handle-relative binaries: test::process_run resolves its executable against a workspace handle and accepts only relative paths alongside argv/cwd/env/options. Absolute paths and ../ escapes refuse, so runnable binaries are exactly those under the sealed workspace root; the handle is the trust boundary, with no registry involved.

process_dispatch.instructions: Select the spawn shape under which staged offline tool runs with cwd/env/argv/limits and descendant cleanup stay expressible yet arbitrary dispatch/eval stays unrepresentable.

criteria.no_workspace_ops: Convention only: no operations are added, tests keep passing raw paths to files::*, and staging plus cleanup rest on caller discipline. Zero mechanism, zero enforcement, and no observable cleanup receipt.
criteria.opaque_handle: Scoped handle plus relative paths: test::workspace_open allocates a fresh grant-owned directory behind an opaque non-constructible handle, fresh test::* file operations address handle-plus-relative-path, and test::workspace_close seals the directory and arranges cleanup. Forgery fails table lookup, staleness fails liveness lookup, absolute/escaping paths refuse; the grant/channel handle discipline extends naturally.
criteria.root_path_string: Bare root string: a single new test::workspace_root operation discloses the fresh directory as str, after which tests continue with files::* over joined paths. One operation total, but the isolation boundary is purely advisory since files::* accepts arbitrary paths.

workspace_model.instructions: Select the scratch-directory shape that isolates tests and guarantees cleanup without ambient file access at minimal mechanism cost.
